subject: Renewal: Dedicated reserved pool expansion — isolation & throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kaplan <sarah.kaplan@acme-retail.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acme-retail.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com, dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated reserved pool expansion — isolation & throughput guarantees

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the heads-up that ACME is preparing the renewal packet. Per our last call, you indicated wanting to expand the Dedicated pool from 16 -> 40 A100-equivalent GPUs and to formalize tenant separation guarantees as part of the renewal terms. I attached a draft SOW with the proposed capacity increase and a network-segmentation sketch.

High-level summary of what we're proposing here: 
- Reserved pool: additional 24 GPUs added to your Dedicated pool, billed as part of the annual commit.
- Isolation: logical tenant separation with dedicated namespaces and network ACLs; optional physical isolation (separate node groups) for additional fee.
- Throughput SLAs: target 99th percentile decoding latency under agreed QPS; throughput floor of X tokens/s per pool to be guaranteed in the contract addendum.

Before we finalize numbers and the DocuSign package, you asked for concrete confirmation that other tenants will not share the same GPU instances and what that means operationally. Looping in Dev (dev_patel) to confirm the technical plan and the operations steps to enforce the isolation.

Next steps:
1) Dev to confirm isolation options and propose the minimal steps for procurement sign-off.
2) I’ll update the SOW (attached) with the final GPU counts and pricing, and produce a DocuSign envelope once we align.
3) If procurement needs a different billing cadence or PO wording, let me know — we can add a 60-day notice clause or adjust the term dates.

Attachments: Acme_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW draft), network_segmentation-draft.png

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated reserved pool expansion — isolation & throughput guarantees

Thanks Marissa — adding technical details here.

Short answer: yes, we can provide the level of isolation ACME is requesting. Options (trade-offs summarized):

1) Logical isolation (default; no hardware change) — Dedicated tenant namespaces, per-customer config enforced in the orchestration layer, KV/prefix caching scoped per-tenant, and strict network ACLs. This prevents cross-tenant request mixing at the runtime level.
  - Pros: fast to provision (hours), lower cost.
  - Cons: if ACME needs hardware-level guarantees for compliance, logical isolation may not be sufficient for legal procurement.

2) Physical isolation (recommended for high-assurance accounts) — spin up a separate node group (reserved host pool) with GPUs dedicated to ACME. No other tenant scheduled onto those nodes.
  - Pros: strongest isolation; easier to articulate in contract ("no co-tenancy on GPU hosts").
  - Cons: longer lead time (~2-4 weeks), incremental hardware cost captured in the SOW.

Throughput & SLA specifics: we can guarantee a throughput floor per pool; example in the attached SOW: minimum sustained throughput of 18k tokens/s for the expanded pool at p95 under the committed instance mix, with a 99th percentile latency target of 220ms for typical 512-token requests when within the reserved pool's capacity. We will include an automatic fallback policy to alternative model variants if the pool crosses 95% utilization to avoid tail latency spikes.

Operational steps to enforce physical isolation (if you pick option 2):
- Provision separate autoscaling group and node labels scoped to ACME.
- Configure scheduler to refuse co-scheduling with other customer namespaces.
- Audit logs and attestations produced monthly; we can include a SOC2 evidence snippet in the contract.

If ACME chooses logical isolation but needs stronger auditability, we can supply monthly attestation reports plus access to per-request trace logs (masked) for a longer retention window as an add-on.

I can prepare the specific AWS/GCP instance type mapping and the exact node count once procurement confirms cloud preference and the final GPU mix.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Kaplan <sarah.kaplan@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acme-retail.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated reserved pool expansion — isolation & throughput guarantees

Marissa / Dev —

Thanks for the quick responses — this is exactly the level of detail we need for procurement and security. A few clarifying points from our side: 
- Procurement will prefer a contract clause that explicitly states "no co-tenancy on GPU hosts" if we opt for physical isolation. Is there standard language you use for that?
- We need the attestation cadence and sample report format to review with our InfoSec team. Monthly is fine, but can you confirm the fields included (IP ranges, node ids, proof of no scheduling events with other tenants, timestamps)?
- On throughput: can you confirm the numbers in the SOW apply after steady-state warmup and exclude cache priming time? We want to avoid SLA disputes during the first week of deployment when caching behavior stabilizes.

If you can provide the contract language and an attestation sample by EOD Monday we’ll take it to our legal and InfoSec for fast-tracked review.

Best,
Sarah Kaplan
Head of AI Platform | Acme Retail

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kaplan <sarah.kaplan@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwoodinference.com, procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated reserved pool expansion — isolation & throughput guarantees

Hi Sarah —

We have standard contract language for physical isolation that procurement can use. I’m pasting the clause below; legal has approved this for prior dedicated deals. Dev, please review and confirm the attestation fields we can commit to.

"Physical GPU isolation: Redwood Inference will provision a dedicated pool of GPU instances for Customer such that no other Redwood customers will be scheduled on the same GPU hosts. Redwood will maintain and provide access to monthly attestation reports identifying node identifiers, host IP ranges, and a signed statement that no cross-tenant scheduling occurred during the reporting period. Customer and Redwood agree that such attestations constitute evidence of isolation for the purpose of this Agreement."

For the attestation fields we typically include: host_id, host_type, host_ip_range, scheduling_events_checked (boolean), timestamp_range, signed_by (ops lead). We redact full request traces but provide summary counts and the audit of scheduler events supporting the attestation. We will also add a clause to exclude the first 7 days from SLA calculations (warmup/caching window) to address your caching concern.

Marissa — once Sarah confirms this wording I’ll ask Legal to produce the amendment and I can get Procurement on a quick call if they want clarifications.

- Rishi
VP, Commercial

Procurement — let me know if you want a 1:1 to walk the amendment. Otherwise we’ll queue this for signature and target a renewal effective date of 2026-03-01.

Best,
Marissa
